purpose: TSDF-fitted structural-plane completion after front-to-back object peeling
promotion_blocker: generative texture and cross-view RGB review remain required; geometry success alone cannot promote a final clean plate

upstream_multiview_prefill.purpose: calibrated multi-view donor prefill before residual video inpainting
upstream_multiview_prefill.lineage_role: measured multi-view donor prefill; planar completion consumes only its residual masks

support_plane.source: Holi structure anchor fixes offset; TSDF fixes Manhattan normal/topology
support_plane.scene_fit_role: gravity/support constraint for grounded object placement

texture_coverage.denominator: original removal-mask pixels across selected frames

planar_completion_patch.role: geometry-only hidden-surface patch; not final textured scene mesh

texture_provenance_contract.measured_texture: only DA3-depth samples outside the current removal mask and within the fitted TSDF plane tolerance
texture_provenance_contract.generative_texture: only generative_texture_masks/*.png; a later model may fill these pixels but must preserve plane geometry and report synthetic provenance
forbidden: painting unresolved_geometry_masks as if geometry were known
using ProPainter blur as structural evidence
reusing old DA3 depth as final reconstructed depth after RGB generation

cumulative_mask_receipt.identity_precedence: supplement residual overrides upstream measured donor prefill

next_stage.texture_generation: fill only generative_texture_masks with geometry-conditioned, plane-coordinate consistent texture; keep measured texels and outside-mask RGB fixed
next_stage.validation: warp accepted texture across calibrated views, reject seams or plane-boundary drift, then rerun depth/normal estimation and PGSR/TSDF

limitations: The method completes planar room structure, not curved or articulated hidden geometry.
A plane can be geometrically complete while its hidden texture remains unobserved.
TSDF and DA3 errors are recorded separately and cannot certify final RGB quality.
